source_evidence.anchor: Paragraph beginning “Recall that a random variable Z has Poisson distribution with parameter λ” and Equation (1.8)
source_evidence.observation: The source defines the notation Z ∼ Pois(λ), states that Z takes values in {0,1,2,...}, and gives P{Z = k} = e^{-λ} λ^k / k! for k = 0,1,2,....

source_evidence.anchor: Immediate paragraph preceding the Poisson definition
source_evidence.observation: The parameter arises as the limiting O(1) mean of sums of Bernoulli random variables; no explicit domain restriction on λ is stated in the definition itself.

The subsequent theorem writes sums of Bernoulli parameters converging to λ < ∞, which implicitly places λ in the nonnegative finite regime, but does not add an explicit lower-bound hypothesis at Equation (1.8).

hypotheses: Z has Poisson distribution with parameter λ, denoted Z ∼ Pois(λ)
conclusions: P{Z = k} = e^{-λ} λ^k / k! for every k = 0,1,2,...
definitions_and_conventions: Pois(λ) denotes the Poisson distribution with parameter λ.
The event in Equation (1.8) is the singleton-value event {Z = k}.
The exponential factor is e raised to the negative parameter, e^{-λ}.
The numerator contains the kth power λ^k.
The denominator is the factorial k!.
Equation (1.8) specifies the probability mass function over all nonnegative integer values k.
implicit_context: The source does not explicitly state λ ≥ 0 or λ > 0 at this definition.
For the displayed quantities to form probabilities of a Poisson law, λ is implicitly a finite nonnegative real parameter.
The source uses ordinary probability notation P and treats Z as a random variable on an unstated probability space.
At λ = 0 and k = 0, interpreting the formula requires the standard convention for the zeroth power; the source does not discuss this edge case.

Z takes values in the nonnegative integers {0,1,2,...}.

It applies to every nonnegative integer k.

contract_plain_english: Equation (1.8) defines the Poisson law: a random variable Z is written Z ∼ Pois(λ) when it is nonnegative-integer-valued and, for every k = 0,1,2,..., the singleton probability that Z equals k is e^{-λ} times λ to the kth power divided by k factorial. The source does not explicitly state λ’s domain at this equation; the surrounding Bernoulli-limit context supports the standard finite nonnegative-real parameter interpretation.
